newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Check out non-bank rates, Costello tells Australia.
newsitem.headline: Check out non-bank rates, Costello tells Australia.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello on Monday urged consumers to look elsewhere if their banks did not fully pass on to them the 0.5 percentage point cut in interest rates effected by the Reserve Bank on Friday.

"If your bank is only offering you 7.2 percent on the standard variable, get down to Aussie Home Loans, or get down to RAMS, or get down to Priority One, and find a financial institution that is offering a better deal," Costello told parliament.
Aussie, RAMS and Priority One are among the new breed of non-bank mortgage lenders whose competition has driven down home loan margins in recent years.
Australia's four biggest banks on Friday cut home loan rates by 0.35 percentage points.
Anti-monopolies authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, said earlier on Monay it would investigate whether the main banks colluded in cutting home loan interest rates.
Commission chief Allan Fels said that it was unusual for all the big banks to cut interest rates by the same amount at the same time.

Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ), National Australia Bank and Westpac Banking Corp all cut their standard variable home loan rates to 7.20 percent from 7.55 percent.
